title: Unsigned labelled-tail deletion correspondence
statement:
Let $I$ be a linearly ordered type, $p\in\mathbb N$, $n=p+2$, and $t:\operatorname{Fin}(n)\to I$. Use the stable sorts, partial sorts, and junction maps of [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators]. Write $q_{\sigma,\tau,a}=\operatorname{cechJunction}(\sigma,\tau,a)$ and $\delta_j=j.\operatorname{succAbove}$ for the increasing map omitting $j$. Let $O_t$ be the set of quadruples $(\sigma,a,\tau,r)$, with $\sigma,\tau\in S_n$, $a\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)$, such that $\sigma$ stably sorts $t$, $\tau$ partially sorts $\sigma$ with prefix length $a$, $q_{\sigma,\tau,a}(r)\ne\sigma(a)$, and $r\ge a$. Let $D_t$ be the set of quadruples $(j,\rho,b,\eta)$, with $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, $\rho,\eta\in S_{n-1}$, $b\in\operatorname{Fin}(n-1)$, such that $\rho$ stably sorts $t\circ\delta_j$, $\eta$ partially sorts $\rho$ with prefix length $b$, and it is not the case that $t(j)<t(\delta_j(\rho(b)))$ or that $t(j)=t(\delta_j(\rho(b)))$ and $j<\delta_j(\rho(b))$. Then there exists an equivalence $e:O_t\simeq D_t$ such that for every $x=(\sigma,a,\tau,r)$, writing $e(x)=(j,\rho,b,\eta)$, there exists $k\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ with
$$k+1=r,\qquad \tau(k)=j,\qquad \tau\circ\delta_k=\delta_j\circ\eta,\qquad a=b,\qquad q_{\sigma,\tau,a}\circ\delta_r=\delta_j\circ q_{\rho,\eta,b}.$$
The position equality $a=b$ is an equality of natural-number values. This statement concerns only finite indices and maps; it has no coefficients or cochain values.

lean.statement:
theorem cechTailDeletionCorrespondence {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (p : ℕ)
    (t : Fin (p + 2) → I) :
    ∃ e : cechTailOutgoingIndex p t ≃ cechTailIncomingIndex p t,
      ∀ x, ∃ k : Fin (p + 2),
        k.val + 1 = x.val.2.2.2.val ∧
        x.val.2.2.1 k = (e x).val.1 ∧
        (∀ z, x.val.2.2.1 (k.succAbove z) =
          (e x).val.1.succAbove ((e x).val.2.2.2 z)) ∧
        x.val.2.1.val = (e x).val.2.2.1.val ∧
        cechJunction x.val.1 x.val.2.2.1 x.val.2.1 ∘ x.val.2.2.2.succAbove =
          (e x).val.1.succAbove ∘
            cechJunction (e x).val.2.1 (e x).val.2.2.2 (e x).val.2.2.1
